learning_outcomes.text: Understand the behavior of elastic materials.
Understand and use mathematical techniques to calculate the stress state of an elastic body.
Understand and use mathematical techniques to calculate the deformation state of an elastic body.
Understand and use mathematical techniques that relate the stress and deformation states of an elastic body.
Know how to apply elasticity for the two-dimensional case.
Provide the fundamental hypotheses and concepts that allow for the assimilation of the resistant behavior of different structural systems and elements.
Know the traditional methods used in the calculation of bar structures.
Know the equilibrium method: the matrix formulation of the direct stiffness method.

syllabus_topics: Stress state of an elastic medium.
Deformation state of an elastic medium.
Relationship between stress and deformation states.
General formulation of the elastic problem.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of two independent parts (Elasticity and Theory of Structures), both of which must be passed. Compensation is possible from a score of 2 out of 5 in one of the parts. Practical work will only be considered for the final grade if a score higher than 4.5 in the written exam is obtained. For multiple-choice questions, two incorrect answers will subtract the value of one correct answer. If the problem statement is correct but the result is incorrect due to calculation errors, up to 50% of the question's value may be awarded. Incorrectly expressed units will result in a deduction of 0.1 points for every 5 errors.
